name: Pu Luong rice terraces: Kho Muong to Ban Hieu
region: Pù Luông Nature Reserve, Bá Thước, Thanh Hóa
why: Two days on village paths through a limestone valley: rice terraces, bamboo water wheels and Thai stilt houses, with a night in a homestay and a swim under the Hiêu falls at the end.
book: No permit. Shared vans from Hanoi's Old Quarter reach Pu Luong in 4-5 hours, some via Mai Châu. Book a stilt-house homestay in Bản Đôn for the night; local guides are recommended for the longer routes. Arrange a car or motorbike back from Bản Hiêu.
water: Drinks and meals in the villages and homestays along the way. Carry 1.5 litres between villages.
dangers: Clay paths and paddy dykes are slippery in the rainy season: good walking shoes.
Heat and humidity in May, June and September: start early.
Parts of the route follow village roads with motorbikes.
Stay on the paths through the terraces: they are farmed fields.
turnaround: No hard turnaround: every village on the way is on a road, so you can stop and ride on.

points.name: Kho Muong
points.note: A remote Thai village in a bowl of limestone mountains, next to the Kho Muong cave. The path climbs out south over a pass towards the main valley.

points.name: Pu Luong terraces at Ban Don
points.note: Night in a stilt-house homestay. Rice terraces climb the slopes all around: green in May and June, golden in September and October.

points.name: Paddies and water wheels at Lan Trong
points.note: Day 2 follows the valley floor past the paddies of Lăn Trong, where bamboo water wheels lift water from the stream to the fields.

points.name: Ban Hieu waterfall
points.note: The Hiêu falls drop over several limestone steps into clear pools where you can swim, beside the Thai village of Bản Hiêu.
